analysis.investment_thesis: BLS International is a rare find in Indian markets — a capital-light services business with 34% ROE, 34% ROCE, 23.7% operating margins, and a net profit CAGR of 37.4% over nine years, all trading at a reasonable 19x trailing and 15x forward P/E. The visa/passport outsourcing model carries genuine switching-cost moat because government diplomatic missions cannot easily change service providers once embedded, and geographic expansion compounds the advantage.
key_strengths: ROE of 34.3% and ROCE of 33.6% — outstanding capital efficiency sustained over many years
FCF of INR 668 Cr in FY2025 exceeds net profit of 540 Cr — excellent earnings quality and cash conversion
19x trailing and 15x forward P/E is genuinely reasonable for a business compounding profits at 37% CAGR
key_risks: Massive FY2025 acquisition (investing outflow INR 1,119 Cr, total assets nearly doubled) — integration risk and unknown acquisition quality
Borrowings surged from INR 31 Cr to INR 404 Cr — debt-funded acquisition changes the risk profile
Revenue is partly government-contract dependent; a single large contract loss can cause step-down in earnings
red_flags: FY2025 investing cash outflow of INR 1,119 Cr — a transformative acquisition with limited public detail warrants scrutiny
Finance costs jumped from INR 8 Cr to INR 47 Cr, compressing the otherwise exceptional margin profile
DII holding is only 2.92% — relatively undiscovered or institutional conviction is limited
analysis.detailed_analysis:
BLS ticks most of the boxes I care about: an asset-light business model (visa/consular processing requires regulatory approvals and government relationships, not factories), exceptional returns on capital, growing free cash flow that exceeds reported earnings, and a reasonable price. The 9-year track record of 17.7% revenue and 37.4% profit CAGR is not a fluke — it reflects compounding geographic expansion across India and international markets.

The single significant concern is the FY2025 acquisition — total assets doubled from INR 1,616 Cr to INR 3,339 Cr, and borrowings grew 13-fold. Berkshire has made large acquisitions too, and I don't oppose them if the acquired business strengthens the moat. The underlying pre-acquisition business quality is excellent, and at 15x forward earnings, I am not paying a premium for uncertain outcomes. I would want to understand the acquisition before committing fully, but the core business deserves a position.
